messages:
mike: Heads-up — customer request for per-tenant canaries on Dedicated. They want 5% traffic for 48h, but also hard quotas & isolation. How do we reasonably expose this in the API/Console without letting users shoot themselves in the foot?

tara: do we mean two things: traffic split for rollout vs. quota caps for cost/overload protection?

mike: yes — both. They want to run A/B within their tenant slice and also enforce a cap so canary can't consume >X GPUs or tokens.

liam: operational constraints first: dedicated pools are shared by slice but still need tenant isolation. We currently have per-tenant rate limiter + cluster-level circuit breaker. We should avoid a canary operator being able to increase qps beyond their reserved capacity.

nina: UX suggestion: Console exposes a "Canary rollout" wizard with two knobs: % traffic (0.1%–100%) and "Max resource budget" (tokens/hour or GPU-minutes). Default budget = 10% of tenant's committed capacity. Also option to auto-pause on error-rate spike.

kevin: API side: propose a rollout object: 
```
POST /v1/rollouts
body: { tenant_id, variant_a, variant_b, split: 0.05, duration: "48h", budget: { tokens_per_hour: 1e6, gpu_minutes: 60 }, safeguards: { max_error_rate: 0.05, fallback: "route-to-stable" } }
```
Admin keys required to create budgets above commit.

mike: +1 to requiring admin approval for budgets > commit. What about telemetry? We need to show live traffic and per-variant latencies + cost.

liam: we'll need per-route + per-variant metrics in the Console: p50/p95 latency, token/sec, token-cost estimate, and a green/yellow/red health flag based on error-rate and latency regressions. Easiest is to reuse our existing per-model traces but tag by rollout_id.

nina: small UX detail: show estimated spend burn rate for the canary over the duration and an optional hard kill switch in the top-right of the rollout page. Customers like single-click abort.

kevin: on enforcement: implement two checks at routing time: 1) Allocation check — only allow requests routed if tenant's budget not exceeded. 2) Circuit-breaker — if model latency/error threshold breached for variant, automatically divert remaining canary traffic to stable. Both are cheap checks in the routing layer.

mike: what about test isolation? We must prevent canary cache pollution for other tenants (KV cache). Any ideas?

liam: we already namespace KV caches by tenant and variant id; but prefix reuse can increase memory. For short-lived canaries, TTL shorter and aggressive cache eviction is fine. Also allow an opt-in mode where canary uses a separate model instance pool if they request hard isolation (higher cost).

nina: console should label canaries that use "hard isolation" and show premium pricing warning.

kevin: rolling back: provide both automated rollback (on threshold breach) and manual rollback API that sets split to 0 and triggers warm-pool drain for canary variant. We'll emit events to the audit log.

mike: sounds good. Edge case: two overlapping canaries for same tenant on same route. Should we allow?

liam: deny overlapping canaries by default; allow operator override with explicit precedence ordering. Overlaps cause split math confusion.

nina: +1. Add a warning in the UI if tenant tries overlapping.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-service:v2.4.1 scheduled to canary cluster at 2024-06-02T15:30Z; migration: rollout_schema bump.

mike: thanks — can someone PR a spec for the API shape + console mockups? I'll collect compliance notes for enterprise customers (audit record, KMS keys, admin approval).

kevin: I'll sketch the API and enforcement flow, pinging @tara for RBAC requirements.

tara: will draft RBAC + approval gate. Also add rate-limiter rule to deny budget > commit.

mike: great. Let's aim for an RFC by EOW. :thumbsup:
